# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

## v0.1.1

### Features

- **Module permissions system**: modules can now opt into outbound HTTP access by declaring `"permissions": ["web"]` in
  their manifest — shown to you as a confirmation before install, same idea as a mobile app permission prompt, rather
  than every module silently having it (or none of them ever being able to).
- **Generic Twitch EventSub subscriptions**: modules can now declare which Twitch events they care about (follows, subs,
  raids, a native poll starting, etc.) instead of the app only ever watching for channel-point redemptions. The app
  keeps exactly one EventSub connection and subscribes to each distinct event type once, no matter how many installed
  modules want it, and automatically adds/removes subscriptions as modules get enabled or disabled.
- Added `twitch.pin_message()` / `twitch.unpin_message()` for scripts — pins a chat message via Twitch's own pin feature
  (20-minute fixed duration).
- Added `twitch.end_poll()` — lets a script end a native Twitch poll early.
- Added `ms.after(seconds, script_key)` — a module script can now schedule a delayed re-run of one of its own scripts,
  useful for anything that needs to check back on something later without blocking the command that triggered it.
- Added `ms.overlay_url()` / `ms.resource_url()` — resolve one of a module's own overlay pages or bundled resource files
  to a stable, correctly-namespaced URL, without the module having to build that URL itself.
- Module overlay/resource serving now covers plain bundled assets (images, etc.), not just overlay HTML pages — and
  those assets can be used directly as icons anywhere in the app's UI, including sidebar/tab icons.
- Settings forms can now put a compact control (like a unit toggle) directly on a field's label row instead of giving it
  a whole separate row, and can group fields for spacing without necessarily showing a visible section header.

### Improvements

- Per-row list icons (previously hardcoded to just Twitch/YouTube) now work for any module-provided icon, not only the
  two built-in chat platforms.
- List selection no longer freezes at the moment you click a row — it now stays in sync with live data and clears itself
  cleanly if that row gets removed.
- Live updates from a module's own scripts now actually reach the UI without needing a manual reload — previously only
  two specific built-in signals triggered a refresh, so a module using its own custom live-update event had no way to
  make the screen update on its own.
- Native Twitch polls now show live vote counts while the poll is still running, instead of only once it's fully closed.

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed password-type fields in settings forms showing their contents in plain text instead of masked.
- Fixed dropdown fields sometimes showing the wrong option while their real saved value was still loading, instead of a
  clear "loading" state.
- Fixed a settings-form bug where one slow or failing field could cause every other field on the same form to silently
  show a placeholder instead of your actual saved value.
- Fixed a module install/update bug where a module's own bundled helper scripts could silently stop updating after the
  first install.
- Fixed a routing bug where certain parameterized API routes could fail to match at all.
- Fixed a stale version check that compared against a hardcoded build number instead of the app's actual running
  version.

## v0.0.9

### Bug Fixes

- **Nightly Release 0.0.9**: ## Bug Fixes
- removed `await win.setFocus()` from both **show-level-nexted** and **show-level-copied** handlers (was stealing focus
  on every overlay show)
- background GD fetch now emits `level-nexted-gd` instead of `re-emitting level-nexted`. The original emission already
  showed the overlay; the second one was re-showing it seconds later (timed exactly when you'd be browsing history)
- `level-nexted-gd` is forwarded to the overlay as `show-level-nexted-gd`, which silently updates the GD name element
  in-place with no `win.show()` or countdown reset
